what_was_done: The spec and check parts hold: --subject is gone from the four script texts, checkpoint_calls_match_the_signature fails on a re-added --subject and on the old toy form '--outcome ${outcome.status}', and the SL1-51 test fails when gated()'s stage passthrough is dropped. Two parts are still wrong. (1) toy-story.js regressed. Its close is now `${outcome && outcome.status === 'failed' ? ' --outcome failed' : ''}`, and outcome is undefined when gated() throws, so a thrown run closes WITHOUT --outcome failed. Run through the harness with a throwing implementer, the clerk prompt is 'vsdd -C /proj checkpoint toy-story --run r1 --json'. HEAD passed --outcome failed there, and story-script.md passes failed=true from its catch. No test catches this: the check reduces every non-`${failed...}` ternary to a placeholder, and the only behavioural test throws inside toy-build. (2) The reopened AU-P2-12 never reaches the packages it names. findings.py routes a triaged finding by triage/d.json, which still lists packages B1, B2, H2 and S1 and the four files already repaired. So by-package/E2.md, E3.md and S2c.md do not carry it, and the H2 list shows 'Files: packaging/cli-entry.md, packaging/plugin-manifest.md, rules/secrets.md, tables/limits.toml'. The outcome also names a file that does not exist (topics/proof-greenfield.md; the file is packaging/proof-greenfield.md, owned by E3, which it does not name). The registry gives topics/rule-testing, risks-hooks and information-walls no package, so 'the H packages (H1-H9)' routes nowhere. These six pointer replacements are spec text edits that no later package is needed for. Proposed fix: in toy-story.js pass --outcome failed when outcome is null as well (`!outcome || outcome.status === 'failed'`), and add a harness test that a thrown toy-story run's close carries --outcome failed. Then either repair the stale pointers in the six files now (rule-testing.md:11, risks-hooks.md:9, information-walls.md:74, packaging/e2e-story-tier.md:20,37, packaging/proof-greenfield.md:23-24, commands/status.md:18) and mark AU-P2-12 fixed, or have the orchestrator update triage/d.json so AU-P2-12 lists those files and their real owner packages, with the path corrected.

The skeletons and toys now pass, and TestSpecSkeletons fails if the adoption exception is removed. But probes through workflow_problems show the fix is too broad in one place and too blind in others. (1) RUN_TIER_ADOPTION_RE accepts any identifier chain, not 'exactly the two forms the skeletons use': `RUN.tier = TIER.planner`, `RUN.tier = TIER.reviewer || null` and `RUN.tier = a.tier || TIER.planner` all pass, so a hand-written region can pin the whole run to a tier, which is the thing the rule forbids. The fixer's account says '|| null' is required; the regex does not require it. (2) _strip_comments_and_strings blanks the whole of a template literal, interpolations included. So `${await agent('x', {})}`, `${step(..., { model: 'opus' })}` and `${await workflow('vsdd-factory:release', {})}` inside a template are not reported, though a raw scan caught them. A regex literal containing a quote (`s.replace(/'/g, '')`) throws the stripper's string state off, and a following direct `await agent('x', {})` is not reported. (3) No test pins the stripping: replacing `js = _strip_comments_and_strings(body)` with `js = body` passes all 79 lint tests. (4) The data-key false positive the finding named, `{ model: u.model }`, is still rejected. Proposed fix: match the two adoption forms exactly (`RUN.tier = a.tier || null` and `RUN.tier = s.config.tier_override || null`, or a member chain on a/s ending in `|| null` that names no TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE). Make the stripper scan `${...}` bodies as code, and treat a regex literal as opaque or else fail closed. Add tests that a comment `// the agent (x)` and a string 'effort: high' are not reported, that agent( and a forbidden workflow( inside `${}` are, and that `RUN.tier = TIER.planner` is. Decide whether `{ model: u.model }` is allowed and test it either way.

The either-or restatement is gone, but the replacement sentence leaves a parenthesis open: '... and is defined in that table ([[rule:spike-bounds]]. Two cases hold it: ...'. The ')' that closed the old clause was dropped, so the next sentence reads as if it were inside the parenthesis. spec_lint does not catch it. Proposed fix: close it, '([[rule:spike-bounds]]). Two cases hold it:', or make it the bare link to the own-worktree definition in [[table:path-classes]] that the finding asked for.

Mostly earned now: changing the contract row's glob, id, dir, cap, writer, lock, template or any frontmatter cell fails TestContractArtifactKind, and all seven story-kind rows' stage cells and red_gate are pinned (harness verifier->implementer, proofs->fuzzing, facade red_gate and port tests_method each fail). But the contract row's headings cell, the BC sections the artifacts rule enforces on write, is unpinned: dropping 'Test vectors' (or emptying the list) passes test_policy.py, test_roster_lint.py and check.py. The header still says the [contract] row is pinned, and the story row's headings are asserted (test_policy.py:309). Proposed fix: assert row['headings'] == ['Behavior', 'Preconditions', 'Postconditions', 'Invariants', 'Edge cases', 'Test vectors'] in TestContractArtifactKind, or narrow the header's claim.

The enum is pinned: dropping checkout_dirty fails valid_state-checkout-dirty.json, and invalid_unknown-state.json pins the refusal. But three of the new valid fixtures contradict the schema they illustrate. valid_state-ci-failed.json, valid_state-conflict.json and valid_state-review-stale.json have ok: true with a non-empty error ('CI failed on the merge commit.', 'The merge has conflicts.', 'Head moved after the converged verdict.'), while delivery-data.schema.json says error is 'One line a person can act on; empty when ok', and story-deliver.md uses error only for the ok: false states. A builder of vsdd story deliver who copies these fixtures will print an error on success. Proposed fix: set error to '' in those three fixtures. Or, if an actionable line on these ok: true states is intended, change the schema description and story-deliver.md to say so.
